topic: The 'no talent' excuse: we tell ourselves we're just not built for running or lifting and use it as a reason to stop; talent is not ours to choose, but patience, endurance of effort and showing up again need no gift, so we work on those instead
figure: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor and Stoic, 121-180 AD (Meditations 5.5: you say people cannot admire your quick wit; granted, but there are many other qualities of which you cannot say 'I have no gift for it', such as sincerity, dignity, endurance of toil, restraint in pleasures, contentment with little; show those, since they are entirely in your power). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request

lines: เราบอกตัวเองว่า “ไม่มีพรสวรรค์”
